questions.question: Which of these is a usable audience boundary rather than a label?
options: Enterprise team leads who value staying organised across their meetings
Team leads on enterprise contracts in workspaces with more than 500 documents
People who run a recurring meeting series and afterwards write a record that someone who missed the meeting reads
Busy managers who need decisions and action owners to survive handoffs
questions.explanation: C names a repeated behaviour and the context that makes the problem occur, so a recruiter or an analyst could sort a borderline case. B is the tempting distractor because it is precise and queryable, but every term in it is an attribute: it captures billing and workspace size, and large workspaces are the performance population, not necessarily the meeting population.

questions.question: A PM's audience definition excludes nobody. What does that tell you?
options: The definition has no edges, so it is a description of the whole user base with adjectives attached
The opportunity is unusually broad, which strengthens the case for building it
The definition is fine as long as the behaviour named in it is observable
The team should segment after launch, once usage data arrives
questions.explanation: Exclusion is what gives a boundary edges; without it the definition expands until it means everyone. B is the tempting distractor because breadth reads as market size, but an audience that includes everyone cannot be wrong, which means it also cannot inform a design decision or a priority comparison.

questions.question: Meeting type is not captured in the product's event data, and actor identity is missing for about 18% of events. A PM wants to size the meeting-summaries audience. What is the honest move?
options: Estimate the audience from enterprise plan counts and note the estimate as approximate
Build first and instrument the behaviour afterwards, since the data will exist once the feature ships
Model the population from industry benchmarks for meeting frequency
Try a behavioural proxy and state its error direction; if none holds, declare the population size unobservable rather than estimating it
questions.explanation: The preference order is observable proxy with a stated error direction, then a screening question, then declaring it unobservable — which is a legitimate answer. A is the tempting distractor: an approximate number from plan counts substitutes what you can produce for what you need, and "approximate" is stripped off in the first re-quote.

questions.question: A team must ship a capability only for customers whose data has to stay in one jurisdiction. Someone objects that this is an attribute, not a behaviour. Who is right?
options: The objector — attribute-based audiences always hide the behaviour that causes the problem
The team — the attribute is the actual constraint here, and translating it into behaviour would lose the thing that determines who is affected
The objector — the boundary should be people who store regulated data, which is behavioural
Neither — jurisdiction is a legal matter and does not require an audience boundary at all
questions.explanation: This is the boundary of the model: use behaviour when behaviour determines whether the problem occurs, and attributes when the attribute determines it. C is the tempting distractor because it performs the behavioural rewrite correctly and still gets it wrong — the requirement attaches to the jurisdiction, not to what the customer does with the data.

questions.question: A designer blends four behaviours observed in four different customer calls into one target user. What is the specific defect?
options: Four calls is too small a sample to define an audience
The blended user should be validated with a survey before being used
The composite is internally consistent in a way no real person is, so it accommodates every proposal and can disconfirm nothing
The behaviours should have been weighted by the contract value of each account
questions.explanation: A composite is assembled from the same intuitions the proposals come from, so design reviews always go smoothly and no proposal is ever ruled out. A is the tempting distractor because sample size is a real concern, but the defect survives at any sample size — adding more calls makes the composite more vivid, not more real.
